items.title: 61520_Teddy Edwards oral history interview
items.q: Black-Dot McGee was the owner at the time. And he had really laid this place out; it was perfect for Jazz, you know.

ctx.x: We went into Lincoln, Nebraska to play...and the next stop was Los Angeles (hah-hah-hah!) at the Club Alabam on Central Avenue between 42nd and 42nd Place. And I never will forget it. We got in in the middle of...oh, somewhere about 11:30 or 12 o'clock. And Central Avenue was just full of people. All kind of things were happening, you know. They had The Last Word across the street, and Dynamite Jackson's down the street.

They had the Downbeat on 42nd and Central, which is my all-time favorite Jazz club that I played in, because it was really made for it. Black-Dot McGee was the owner at the time. And he had really laid this place out; it was perfect for Jazz, you know.
